# XF recipe — source-side classes renderers and KB auditors kept finding after policy PASS in earlier runs

Every point applies to every extended policy. Instantiators: satisfy each before delivering. Policy auditors: check each point on each policy; any member is RED, not an observation.

1. Factor independence. Each factor contributes on its own against a quantity the baseline defines. No factor tier reads another factor's binding or output, transitively (check mechanically what each factor reads). A record selection several parts share is a plain non-factor binding stated once in the rule. A factor-only quantity belongs to that factor; the baseline defines no quantity only factors use.
2. Assembly. `result` (and plain bindings) assemble the amount. The rule states the combination ONCE, generically, without naming factor quantities ("the adjustments below are applied to the standard amount" — not "points from the four schedules below are added", not "credits after the rate has been applied"). No factor is gated through another factor. No rule phrase defines a quantity "as another policy figures it".
3. Non-commuting order. Wherever adjustments do not commute, the generic combination sentence still fixes their order (e.g. "replacements first, then caps, then additions"), or a second reading appears.
4. compute_basis quotes. Every compute_basis quote is verbatim in its own rule (check_extended does NOT check this — run a scratch sweep).
5. Overwrite hygiene. (a) replaced_by restates the still-in-force content of the retired clause for out-of-scope cases and names its own scope ("for a term this policy … and only for such a term; every other … remains under …" restated); (b) no overwrite that retires nothing or retires clauses that never conflicted; (c) sibling overwrites retiring the same clause each exclude the other's case by name; (d) an extended rule contradicting an in-force base clause with no overwrite is RED; (e) no rule defers to a base clause its own overwrite retires; (f) an undeclared departure from any base sentence is RED.
6. Rounding. The rule's rounding sentence matches the RND placement in compute exactly.
7. Docstrings. No docstring claims an effect the tool body lacks. No concrete example values in docstrings or param descriptions (format only) — an example has equalled gold before.
8. Edges, stated in the rule and probed on a scratch copy: absent record, negative lag, None, zero division; decoy rows (cancelled, voided, reversed, prior-term, second holding, later-dated) for every CFIELD / first-match / LATEST read; same-day tie rule stated (which row LATEST keeps); month-end convention for whole-month/year counts vs MONTHS(); every date-difference boundary (inclusive/exclusive) stated in words matching the compute.
9. Ladders. No tier gaps or overlaps across the real domain; every tier re-checked against the policy's own scope; ≥3 tiers.
10. Method shape. A `method` factor changes the formula's shape, not a multiplier or window length. Pair test: count any aggregate of the same field as one input whatever its window/filter and ignore constant multipliers; a pair FAILS if it is the same combination of the same windowed sums, PASSES if one tier adds an input or an operation (floor, max/conditional pick, data-selected window, tariff parameter). A "nothing" tier fails where another tier is also 0 across its whole domain. Keep a pairwise tier table with a distinguishing input.
11. Rule words == compute in every case. No rule word for a field the records lack. Each factor's text names the result it modifies.
12. DSL limits (exact-value filters; windows run from today; CFIELD = first match; XSUM/XCOUNT over EVENT tables across all the customer's holdings; no holding count; no cross-record date pairing). Do not describe in words a case the compute does not price. Accepted routes: key the read on a record tied to the event by an exact value; scope via a self-naming overwrite to a single live holding and use a two-date DAYS test inside the scope (out of scope gets the BASE figure, computed); aggregate across holdings from event rows. Rejected routes: words-only multi-record cases, pricing switched by an incidental COUNT, "first listed".
13. Cross-category seed realism. Every seeded row of another product must be a state its owning charter can produce, priced with that charter's own formulas (premium, installment amounts, fees, fee shares), with complete ledgers (every billable row invoiced, every periodic event reproducible from the records, signed forms / statements / notices behind every row that needs one).
14. Trigger rule. List every event your tools write with its base `triggers`; none may land in another category.
15. Names. No factor id may be a substring of any tool name. Prerequisite sentences are record tests or state-form waits — never "if policy X would compute …".
16. Realism. Factors are rules a real nonstandard auto carrier uses (state DMV/financial-responsibility law as actually written, or explicitly the company's own schedules). Never invent statutes or tiers keyed on trivia (loyalty counts, ZIP digits).
17. (added round 2) Realism of factor KEYS. Prefer real rating/billing/claims dimensions: liability package, state (real statutory caps, notice days, total-loss tests, FL glass), certificate form/type and backing type, plan and payment method, driver violation points tiers and driver class, days-based methods (pro rata vs short rate vs fully earned), payee/lien position, recovery share. A ladder keyed on incidental counts (copies issued, payments made, endorsements, lapse-fee counts), on who rejected a filing, on a past paid claim cutting a refund, or stacking a company add-on onto a statutory maximum is RED. A company schedule is acceptable only where a real carrier publishes one for that very charge.
18. (added round 2) A status stamp field (e.g. a term's financial_responsibility_filing) that names the same tier a factor derives from other records makes the factor's evidence redundant — derive the tier from a record the stamp does not already state, or key on the stamp honestly as the source.
19. (added round 2) Edge sentences must be no weaker or stronger than the condition they ground (a stale earlier record must not satisfy them), and two policies' gates/edges must not deadlock on any reachable world.
20. (added round 3) Zero-amount edges. A depended-on write whose figure can be 0.00 on a reachable world leaves the blocked side waiting forever if the producing tool requires a positive amount (check the db_schema field meaning before any "post a 0.00 line" idea — it is usually not allowed). Make the zero impossible with a realistic cap/floor in the depended-on rule, or carve the zero case out of the blocked side's wait with a record test.
21. (added round 3) Look-backs. Every priced row's look-back window (12-month returned items, prior terms, points windows) must fall inside seeded records — seed the holding's history from inception where a window reaches back.
22. (added round 3) Removing beats adding. When a factor is struck for realism, do not replace it with a new company add-on; prefer a real dimension already in the records, or choose a different computation. Never charge one rating dimension twice in one charge.
23. (added round 3, coordinator realism bar — applies to reworkers AND auditors) The factor floor is met honestly by rooting amounts in the carrier's RATING PLAN, which is where real nonstandard auto carriers publish many factors. A factor keyed on a dimension that appears in real nonstandard auto rate filings — liability package/limits, state/territory, driver violation/accident points tiers, years licensed / age class, prior insurance lapse, prior cancellation for nonpayment, SR-22/FR-44 filer status, payment plan / EFT or paid-in-full, policy term length — applied to a premium-derived amount (term premium, a driver's rating share, a pro-rata/short-rate return, an installment built from premium) is realistic; its specific numbers may be the company's own filed relativities and must be stated as such. Statutory figures (returned-check caps, notice days, total-loss thresholds) must be the real statute's figure — if unsure, do not cite a statute. RED under point 17 are: fees/credits keyed on incidental counts or on dimensions no filing uses for that very charge, add-ons stacked on statutory amounts, one dimension charged twice, and retaining premium for days with no exposure.
24. (added round 4, coordinator) Flat service charges. Returned-item fees, late fees and SR-22/FR-44 filing fees are charged flat (or at the statutory figure) by real carriers; do not build a 4–6-factor computation on them out of incidental keys. Choose computations that genuinely vary instead (premium-derived billing amounts: installment premium portions, plan-switch re-spreads, down payments, cure/makeup amounts; statutory or state-schedule day counts: SR-26 run-off after the state's receipt, notice days). Where a service charge or a day count does vary, the only acceptable keys are those the company would publish for that service: state (statute or the company's state schedule), certificate form and type, backing type, transmission channel the state requires (electronic vs paper/mail), how coverage ended. Auditors: apply exactly this.
25. (added round 4, coordinator clarification of 24) A service charge or day count built ONLY from the publishable keys listed in point 24 (state or the company's state schedule, certificate form and type, backing type, filing state vs residence/garaging state, how coverage ended or was restored, and the transmission channel where the base lets it vary) is NOT padding, even when it carries 4–6 factors; padding means incidental keys (ledger counts, requirement days remaining, prior-filing-reason surcharges, limits/plan keys on a filing fee). Three-tier ladders may group real values (e.g. FR-44 states / SR-22-only states / out-of-region; owner / operator / owner-operator). Each dimension once.
26. (added round 4) A factor is not load-bearing if a recorded amount the agent can read already embeds it (e.g. a term's recorded full-term premium equal to the rate-plan product, a driver's recorded rating share). Factors must act on what the records do not already embed — a change since the recorded figure (a certificate added after binding, a driver re-rated now), or the transaction's own method — or the recorded figure must not exist in a realistic world.
27. (added round 5, coordinator rulings for filings) (a) The backing term's cancellation reason and the certificate's standing with the state are two dimensions. (c) Lapse length may key "how coverage was restored". (b) The filing state's own group (the state that receives the filing/SR-26) is a dimension only if no other factor is derivable from it together with another factor's key (an out-of-state grade must then compare a different pair, e.g. filing state vs residence state, or be dropped).
